entities.summary:
Epicharmus of Kos was a Greek dramatist and philosopher who lived between 550 and 460 BC. His works are thought to have been written in the Doric or Sicilian comedic form, making him one of the first comedic writers in Western literature. Born on the island of Cos, Epicharmus traveled extensively throughout the ancient Greek world, influencing the development of comedy and philosophy.

Epicharmus's most famous work is 'The Hippias,' a comedic dialogue that satirizes the pretensions of intellectuals. His writings also explored themes of nature, the human condition, and the relationship between reason and emotion. Despite the passing of centuries, Epicharmus's legacy as a pioneering comedic writer and philosopher continues to be felt in the study of Western literature and philosophy.

In addition to his literary contributions, Epicharmus's philosophical ideas have had a lasting impact on Western thought, influencing the development of Stoicism and Epicureanism. His emphasis on the importance of reason, self-control, and living in accordance with nature has made him a central figure in the history of Western philosophy.
